n: Before more judgments fall, John sees four angels at the four corners of the earth holding back the winds of destruction. D&C 77 says they have power over the earth’s four quarters to save life or destroy.
Another angel rises from the east carrying God’s seal and cries out to the four angels. D&C 77 identifies him as Elias, who comes to gather Israel and restore all things.

f.w: another angel ascending from the east

f.g: A signet ring’s mark showing ownership and protection.

n: He commands: don’t harm the earth, sea, or trees until God’s servants are sealed on their foreheads, marking them as belonging to Him.

f.w: sealed the servants of our God in their foreheads

n: John hears that 144,000 from all Israel’s tribes are sealed. D&C 77 explains these are high priests ordained from every nation to bring people to the Church of the Firstborn.

f.w: an hundred and forty and four thousand

n: Twelve thousand are sealed from each tribe. Judah is listed first, likely because the Messiah came from Judah. Twelve times twelve times a thousand suggests fulness and completeness.
The list continues with Asher, Naphtali, and Manasseh, using Greek spellings of the Hebrew names.
Simeon, Levi, and Issachar follow. Levi, usually left out of land lists because it had no territory, is included here.
Zebulun, Joseph, and Benjamin complete the twelve. Dan is not listed; the reason is unknown, though many guesses have been made.

f.g: Here probably standing for Ephraim, whose name is otherwise missing.

n: Then John sees an uncountable multitude from every nation, family, people, and language, standing before the throne in white robes, waving palm branches of victory.
They cry out that salvation belongs to God and to the Lamb—it is His gift, not their achievement.
All the angels, elders, and living creatures fall on their faces and worship God.
They praise God with seven words of honor—blessing, glory, wisdom, thanksgiving, honor, power, and might—forever.
An elder asks John who these white-robed people are and where they came from—a teaching question.
John defers to him, and the elder explains: they came through great tribulation and washed their robes white in the Lamb’s blood. Christ’s Atonement makes people clean.

f.w: made them white in the blood of the Lamb

n: That is why they serve God day and night in His temple, and He will dwell among them, sheltering them with His presence.
They will never again suffer hunger, thirst, or scorching heat—words from Isaiah about the redeemed.
The Lamb will be their Shepherd, guiding them to springs of living water, and God will wipe away every tear from their eyes.
